03 / READING

Opposites attract

Read the text about Cara and Chris.

Do opposites really attract? Or is it better to find someone similar to you? We ask one couple why they are together when they are so different from each other.

OPPOSITES attract

CARA

My boyfriend Chris and I are very different. He’s always out, and he loves playing sports. He likes running, and he loves playing tennis. I don’t mind tennis, but I hate running! I like different activities: I enjoy doing yoga in the park, and I love reading. But I think we’re a great couple. Why? We both like living in the city. We enjoy good restaurants, and we love seeing our friends on the weekend, but I sometimes prefer to spend a quiet evening with him at home.

CHRIS

I think it’s great that Cara and I have our own interests. I enjoy being active: I play tennis and go running every day. Cara enjoys relaxing at home, and she loves visiting museums and galleries. I don’t mind visiting museums, but I hate art! We do some things together – we both love going bowling, for example, but I don’t want a girlfriend who’s just like me. They say “opposites attract,” and I agree!

2A. Read the text about Cara and Chris. What do they do together?

Suggested answersThey enjoy good restaurants, seeing friends on the weekend, and going bowling.

2B. Discuss the questions in pairs.

1. Are Cara and Chris happy that they are very different? Why/Why not?

2. Do you think opposites attract?

Suggested answers1. Yes. Chris says it is great that they have their own interests; Cara thinks they are a great couple. 2. Your own answer.

3A. Read the text again. Complete the sentences.

Suggested answersCara: loves reading; enjoys doing yoga; likes living in the city; doesn’t mind tennis; hates running. Chris: loves playing sports; enjoys being active; likes running; doesn’t mind visiting museums; hates art.
04 / GRAMMAR

Talk about what you like

love, like, hate, enjoy, don’t mind + noun / -ing form

Use these verbs to talk about things you like, dislike, or feel neutral about.

Verb + noun
I love tennis.
I like books.
I hate museums.
Verb + verb-ing
I love playing tennis.
I like reading books.
I enjoy listening to music.

Don’t mind expresses a neutral feeling: I don’t mind playing tennis.

Note: Use a noun or an -ing form after enjoy and don’t mind. Love, like and hate can also be followed by to + verb.

Spelling: adding -ing

play → playing · take → taking · run → running · be → being

06 / MAKE IT YOURS

Speaking & writing

🗣 Speaking

Ask a partner. Answer with a full sentence and give a reason.

What do you love doing on weekends?
What activity don’t you mind doing?
Do you enjoy doing the same activities as your friends?

Example: I love going swimming because it’s fun.

✍️ Writing

Write about yourself and a friend. Use love, like, enjoy, don’t mind and hate with nouns or -ing forms.

Try to write 5–6 sentences. Your writing stays on this page.
